current_answer: Current evidence supports several different routes: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted WebRTC session; Yoroll says YoLive lets a group choose the next scene; Reactor FastH3 uses queued clips and playout; FastVideo documents local FastH3 paths and Dreamverse’s four-GPU frame-carried Preview v1 profile; a community project reports a retimed one-5090 channel; Comfy offers local H3 paths; and vLLM-Omni documents a separate H3 service. The material change is vLLM-Omni’s maintainer-published eight-B300 FastH3 T2VA result: a complete 10.125-second 1344×768 / 24 fps MP4 returned in 8.678 and 8.710 seconds after its excluded warmup. That beats playback at the stated complete-response boundary. It does not prove streaming delivery, time to first frame, cold start, queue capacity, cost, quality, continuity, or viewer-visible interaction; the report says its raw bundle is pending publication. Keep it separate from vLLM-Omni’s earlier four-B300 full-H3 FL2VA row, which returned about 8.71 seconds of output in 86.964 seconds, and from FastH3 8-Step V2’s unresolved ComfyUI FL2VA scope conflict.

catalogue_card.question: Can FastH3 finish a clip before playback ends?
catalogue_card.text: vLLM-Omni says yes for a warmed, dedicated T2VA profile on eight B300 GPUs: 10.125 seconds of MP4 returned in 8.678–8.710 seconds. That is complete-response speed, not a measured live stream.

summary: vLLM-Omni’s maintainer report says an eight-B300, dedicated Dense/Data-Free FastH3 T2VA profile returned a complete 10.125-second 1344×768 / 24 fps MP4 in 8.678 and 8.710 seconds.

The stated timer runs from synchronous submission through complete MP4 receipt. The report defines faster than playback as complete response before media duration, not streaming delivery or time to first frame.
The claim excludes startup, compilation, and an excluded warmup. The raw benchmark bundle is pending publication, so this is not yet independently auditable evidence.

The result is a dedicated T2VA endpoint on eight B300 GPUs. It does not establish FL2VA, frame-carried continuity, browser delivery, queue capacity, concurrency, quality, cost, retries, or viewer-visible response.
uncertainty: vLLM-Omni’s eight-B300 FastH3 result is a maintainer-published, warmed, fixed-profile claim. The pool did not run it, inspect the pending raw bundle, or independently audit its media, environment, quality, or timing.

The complete-MP4 time does not include startup, compilation, or the excluded warmup and says nothing about first frame, streaming, queue, concurrent requests, client delivery, retries, uptime, cost, or viewer-visible latency.
The stated FastH3 route is dedicated Dense/Data-Free T2VA. It does not settle FL2VA, Ref2VA, request-time adapter selection, or a frame-carried continuation workflow.
Dreamverse remains a documented four-GPU frame-carried Preview v1 mechanism, not a measured live-capacity result.
FastVideo and ComfyUI still conflict on FastH3 8-Step V2 first/last-frame FL2VA scope.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end source-to-visible measurement, or first-party pool analytics is available.
